neighboring_unit_entries.title: Joint universality turns analytic independence into orthogonality or matrix rank
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Character orthogonality, full-rank prime-class matrices, arithmetic-progression coefficient means, and Selberg orthogonality are compared, with counterexamples to an overweak criterion.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Continuation alone cannot characterize universal Dirichlet series
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: A general theorem jointly requires independent exponents, continuation, growth, mean square, counting, and coefficient energy; a powers-of-two series refutes the continuation-only conjecture.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Prime phases power ordinary universality but retain zero-free targets; non-Euler-product frequencies support strong universality, which transfers target zeros to source zeros.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Not every series without an Euler product is strongly universal.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Without an Euler-product nonvanishing constraint, Hurwitz zeta can approximate zero-bearing targets; Rouché then converts approximation frequency into linearly many actual zeros.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source states strong universality for Hurwitz zeta when alpha is transcendental or suitable rational, using logarithmic independence or reduction to joint Dirichlet L-functions. It proves that any strongly universal function has at least C T zeros in each interior substrip by approximating s-sigma_0 and applying Rouché's theorem.
directed.conceptual_reading: Removing the nonvanishing target restriction changes approximation into a zero-production mechanism: local topological stability transfers a target's zero to the approximating function.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Frequency independence or the rational character decomposition supplies strong universality, and Rouché's theorem bridges uniform boundary approximation to preservation of interior zero count.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The algebraic irrational Hurwitz case is explicitly open, and the zero lower bound applies only inside the strong-universality region.
directed.uncertainty: The rational decomposition and exact density or strip formulas are formula-dependent, while the Rouché mechanism is clear.

supported: The source states strong Hurwitz universality in the transcendental and suitable rational cases and proves a linear zero lower bound by approximating s-sigma0 and applying Rouche on a small disk.
inference: Removing the nonvanishing target condition genuinely enables zero-bearing targets.
